{{Short description|Statistical modeling methods}}
In [[statistics]], '''large number of rare events''' ('''LNRE''') modeling summarizes methods that allow improvements in [[frequency distribution]] estimation over the [[maximum likelihood]] estimation when "[[rare event]]s are common".<ref name="Department of Linguistics">{{cite web | title=Statistical estimation for Large Numbers of Rare Events | website=Department of Linguistics - Home | url=https://www.ling.upenn.edu/courses/cogs502/LNRE.html | access-date=2019-06-28}}</ref>

It can be applied to problems in linguistics (see [[Zipf distribution]]), in various [[natural phenomena]], in chemistry, in [[demography]] and in [[bibliography]], amongst others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/41336663.pdf|title=Large number of rare events:Diversity analysis in multiple choice questionnaires and related topics|author=Giorgi Kvizhinadze|publisher=A thesis submitted to the Victoria University of Wellington. Victoria University of Wellington|year=2010}}</ref>
